p: "And this is the blessing with which Moshe,
Why Moshe is called "the man of God"
The matter is as brought in the Sifrei (Sifrei Devarim 342),
Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him, finished
from there Moshe began to bless them,
as it says, "And this is the blessing":
וְזֹאת אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר לָהֶם אֲבִיהֶם (בְּרֵאשִׁית מט, כח).
"And this is what their father spoke to them" (Bereishis 49:28).
וְיֵשׁ לְהָבִין מַה זֶּה סִיּוּם בְּרָכוֹת?
Now we must understand: what sort of conclusion of the blessings is this?
After he finished the blessings it says,
"And this is what their father spoke to them,
But this entire pasuk is superfluous,
that this is what their father spoke to them
"each according to his blessing he blessed them,"
דְּאִיתָא בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה צט, ד)
as is brought in the Midrash Rabbah (Bereishis Rabbah 99:4)
that he included them all together in might, etc. —
then it would have sufficed to write,
כָּל אֵלֶּה שִׁבְטֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר
"All these are the tribes of Israel, twelve,
each according to his blessing he blessed them."
אַךְ בֶּאֱמֶת כַּמָּה שְׁבָטִים שֶׁלֹּא בֵּרַךְ:
But in truth there were several tribes whom he did not bless:
and listen to Yisrael your father";
meaning, that his words should enter the heart;
and because he spoke to them
they did teshuvah and merited blessing.
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וְזֹאת אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר לָהֶם:
And this is what it says, "And this is what he spoke to them":
that he instilled in them the attribute of "Zos,"
which is the attribute of Malchus
בְּתִקּוּנֵי זֹהַר קי סוֹף עַמּוּד ד
in Tikkunei Zohar 110, end of the fourth column,
and 111, beginning of the first column,
"And he blessed them" — all of them;
that the words should enter the heart,
and through this they would merit blessing.
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק א קכ, א),
But to his sons, the tribes of Yah,
which is also explicit to the eye,
but it is a feminine form:
the speculum that does not shine.
וְזֶה הָיָה בְּרָכָה אַחֲרוֹנָה שֶׁל יַעֲקֹב
And this was Yaakov's last blessing,
and from it Moshe Rabbeinu began;
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב יְבָמוֹת מט, ב וּבִשְׁאָר מְקוֹמוֹת),
he could give only the attribute of "Zos,"
the speculum that does not shine;
and this is what it says, "And this is the blessing."
for he caused to shine upon Yisrael,
from the attribute of Malchus, the attribute of "Zos."
